title: Active Evaporative Cooling by Ultrasonic Humidification, Refrigeration and Traditional Storage of Potato (Solanum tuberosum L., cv. Spunta) in a Hot Mediterranean Climate: A Reproducible Hierarchy Across Four Campaigns (2022–2025)
content: Storing potato after harvest is challenging in a hot Mediterranean climate, where in-crate temperatures can reach 41–42 °C and cold storage is not always accessible to growers. This study pools four campaigns (2022–2025) at the CTPTA (Tunisia) on cv. Spunta, comparing refrigeration at 7 °C, ultrasonic humidification (H) and traditional greenhouse storage (Trad), testing the reproducibility of their ranking. Storage mode explains 95.5–99.6% of weight-loss variance, and the order 7 °C < H < Trad never inverts across four seasons (mean ω² = 0.981; Mode × Year interaction under 1%). Refrigeration minimises losses (1.86–3.88%) and preserves sanitary quality but triggers cold-induced sweetening beyond the industrial threshold (0.548–0.559%), unsuitable for frying without reconditioning. Humidification keeps sugars low (0.126–0.131%) and limits losses to 3.99–6.36%, cutting them 21–35% relative to the traditional mode, which reaches 5.13–8.63% with 7–18% rot. Skin firmness and titratable acidity (2024) recover the same hierarchy: firmness declines 4.7 times faster under the traditional mode than refrigeration (−1.965 vs −0.416 N/week), and acidity about three times faster (−0.052 vs −0.017 point/week). Sensor monitoring (2024–2025) ranks vapour pressure deficit in the same order (0.12 < 0.89 < 2.22 kPa in 2024), humidification holding the air 6.2 °C and 5.4 °C below the traditional mode and outside temperature at midday. Refrigeration remains the fresh-market reference but requires reconditioning before processing; humidification decouples loss control from technological suitability, offering the most reproducible low-energy option where cold chains are unavailable. Single-site, single-cultivar scope limits external validity.
